# Responses API

Use PLLM's Responses API surface and understand its tested conformance scope.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/integrations/responses-api/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.integrations.responses-api`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:b5c26a66a5b12c51c0db6694ebd66c0925fbb95c68b8048928cf4745a1775861`

Send Responses API requests to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/responses` with a bearer
token for the local gateway. The endpoint supports non-streaming and SSE
streaming text responses, stored response retrieval and cancellation,
continuation with `previous_response_id`, and local function-call items.

`POST /v1/responses/compact` performs bounded local history compaction. It keeps
recent items and marks elided history; it does not ask a provider to generate a
semantic summary.

## Conformance result

The gateway passed all 17 conformance tests from
[OpenResponses](https://www.openresponses.org/) against its 2026-04-24
specification at pinned upstream commit
[`92c12d96d7b61d6d15e2214daa5e9c6000ab6e1c`](https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/commit/92c12d96d7b61d6d15e2214daa5e9c6000ab6e1c).
The run covered the gateway contract exercised by those tests. It does not prove
support for every Responses API field, hosted tool, transport, or model modality.

Current model traffic is text plus local function tools. Image and file inputs
are not model-understood modalities, and provider-built-in tools are not
available. Unsupported fields fail instead of being silently accepted.

Use the [OpenAI Python SDK](/learn/integrations/openai-python/) or
[OpenAI Agents SDK](/learn/integrations/openai-agents/) for tested Python client
paths.

---

# Masked linear inference

Follow seeded one-time masks through offline correction and online matrix evaluation.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/masked-linear-inference/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.masked-linear-inference`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:e307761e359142bb900f5669aa48f929f4ca412891c019495ec5f235a93129c2`

For public matrix `W`, preparation material binds a one-time input mask `r`, output mask `s`, and ticket. Preparation computes `W*r-s` and installs it at inference. Online, the client sends `x-r`; inference combines it with the correction and returns `W*x-s`; the client adds `s`.

This changes timing, not algebra. Reusing a row reveals relations between activations, so each ticket is consumed once. The inference role must never receive the seed, and the preparation role must not retain masks or collude with inference.

Prefill packs a ticket vector and masked matrix per stage. Decode uses one ticket per stage on a persistent connection. See [masked-linear protocol](/sdk/pipeline/protocols/masked-linear/) for the component boundary.

---

# Numeric semantics and model quality

Understand how integer arithmetic affects correctness and model output quality.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/numeric-semantics-and-model-quality/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.numeric-semantics-and-model-quality`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:9f1b3503c3cceb728d1897b5348bd424f0227f147ee7539fd46f0f8c0914eb03`

A model description defines the intended operators. An executable plan must also
choose integer representations, quantization scales, ring widths, nonlinear
approximations, and decoding rules. Each choice can introduce error or overflow.

PLLM selects `u16`, `u24`, or `u32` rings from the maximum signed output of each
prepared stage. This prevents overflow in that stage. It does not show that a
complete generation matches the source model. Quantized token lookup and output
head behavior also depend on the bundle schema and matrix orientation.

Report numeric error, overflow analysis, token agreement, and task quality as
separate results. See [numerics](/sdk/build/numerics/) and
[representations](/sdk/build/representations/).

---

# Parties and offline work

Learn what each party does before and during a private inference request.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/parties-and-offline-work/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.parties-and-offline-work`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:53abc51659043bf19e250a922629dbc0049f9196a8f95d35f217ea8fe996ce92`

The **client** holds plaintext and authorizes each request. The **preparation
service** creates one-time protocol material before a request. The **inference
service** consumes that material while evaluating the model. A **provider**
implements a component. An **operator** controls a deployed process and its policy.

For public-weight inference, preparation commits to the model, transformer body,
stages, quantization, and retry limit. It expands seeds supplied by the client into
input masks, output masks, and one-time tickets. It computes corrections, sends
them to inference, and waits for confirmation. During inference, only the client
and inference service exchange tickets and masked activations.

Reserved rows can be used only once. Cancellation, failure, replay, or early
completion invalidates every unused row in that reservation. See
[preparation](/sdk/pipeline/preparation/) and [deployment](/sdk/operate/deployment/).

---

# Privacy and threat models

Learn what PLLM protects, what each party can see, and which trust assumptions still apply.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/privacy-and-threat-models/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.privacy-and-threat-models`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:b7a2162a110280a1c987c0c1e4621c5e4e3abb5f0a925f24ee1413e6cd4ae3fb`

To evaluate a private inference system, ask six questions:

1. Which values should remain private?
2. Which metadata can each party see?
3. Which parties must follow the protocol?
4. Which parties must not collude?
5. Who receives the output?
6. What evidence supports each answer?

In PLLM's prepared public-weight path, prompts, decoded output, seeds, masks,
private scales, and model state stay with the client. The preparation and inference
services both hold the public transformer body. Preparation receives stage seeds
before inference starts. Inference receives prepared corrections and masked
integer tensors later.

This path assumes that both services follow the protocol and do not collude. If
you run preparation yourself, that trust stays within your own boundary. Two
services controlled by the same operator do not provide meaningful non-collusion.

Authentication and replay controls protect the transport, but they do not protect
against every malicious participant. Timing, traffic volume, public model identity,
tensor shapes, and approximate sequence length may remain visible.

Use [research evidence records](/research/evidence/) to evaluate a specific
privacy claim. Do not infer privacy from the number or names of the services alone.

---

# Reading research and evidence

Learn how PLLM connects papers, clean-room implementations, measurements, and publication claims.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/learn/reading-research-and-evidence/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.learn.reading-research-and-evidence`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:a770dedfe7ec4916dcab45a771035927a905186a407da23e9f8afd45f744aacd`

PLLM records each step from a paper to a published result. It keeps the original
source, clean-room method, component version, plan history, benchmark evidence,
assurance evidence, and proposed claim separate. Citing a paper does not mean it
was reproduced. Passing a unit test does not mean a complete model is supported.
A benchmark does not prove privacy.

Compare results only when the model, model-body fingerprint, plan, numeric policy,
workload, environment, cold or warm mode, and metric definitions match. Keep
limitations and failed attempts in the record. Missing evidence is not a pass.

Continue with [method implementation records](/research/methods/),
[research evidence boundaries](/research/evidence/), and the
[reproduction workflow](/research/recipes/reproductions/).

---

# Metrics

Choose clear performance, resource, quality, and privacy measurements for a PLLM experiment.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/records/metrics/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.metrics`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:193a7b72d5185ed5e1d53cad4f962bbd540874b060b24ac3b628cc01dd041fba`

No single number describes system performance. Report tokens per second, time to
first token, per-token latency, peak and retained memory, CPU time and use,
online and offline network traffic, disk use, preparation work, and failures.
Energy and price require measurements from the stated environment.

Define each metric's scope and denominator. Keep prefill separate from decode,
client from provider, offline from online, cold from warm, and useful output from
attempted work. Record model quality and privacy assurance separately from
performance.

Telemetry must never include prompts, generated text, token IDs, activations,
seeds, masks, or credentials.

---

# Gemma 4

Variant-parameterized text-decoder lowering for exact Gemma 4 E2B and E4B configurations.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/gemma4/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.models.gemma4`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:d809eed88ec2a6edc9fbc7db316f64bdf2be0b8938560123fb75b952afb1d59b`

The Gemma 4 adapter validates exact outer text-decoder contracts for:

| Adapter | Repository revision | Raw configuration SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pllm.gemma4_e2b_text.v1` | `google/gemma-4-E2B-it@3e22461f65e89153144f8adb70e3b8c2cc9845a7` | `1b28f3d2c3100f6c594754b81107428bd7b822a7f48272ca681dae9d2ec38330` |
| `pllm.gemma4_e4b_text.v1` | `google/gemma-4-E4B-it@ee0ef6023621cff504d758262d4e04895a5af4a2` | `33b10c02df3c2e8536cf323d29d53262aaa2f4d11dbe19bc729373fbe90295d4` |

Both plans preserve alternating local/global attention, two head widths, Q/K normalization, PLE, shared-KV suffix state, GeLU-tanh branches, branch-output normalization, and final softcap. E2B additionally doubles effective MLP width in its shared suffix. Variant dimensions and layer schedules are data-driven; compiler paths remain model-neutral.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/gemma-4-E2B-it-3e22461f-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert operations["layer.14.gate_proj"]["output_shape"][-1] == 6144
assert operations["layer.15.gate_proj"]["output_shape"][-1] == 12288
assert operations["layer.34.attention_scores"]["inputs"][1] == "layer.14.key_append"
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the pinned E2B fixture. Lowering does not execute weights.

# Models

See which model configurations PLLM can describe and what model support does not yet include.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.models`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:c58488cb493d34240f862736596c41a4a8a768566a1d46189c75e11cbfb4204e`

`pllm.lower_model(config, batch=..., max_input_tokens=..., max_new_tokens=...)`
turns model configuration and workload limits into a `ModelPlan`. It does not
download weights or tokenizers, choose a device, or start a runtime.

Each adapter validates a specific architecture and produces the same model-neutral
plan format. The plan records operators, layers, weight references, persistent
state, workload limits, and source identity. When a new model needs a new
operation, PLLM extends the shared vocabulary instead of adding model-specific
logic to the compiler.

| Adapter | Validated configuration scope | Added semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pllm.qwen2.v1` | dense Qwen2 configuration contract | grouped-query attention, rotary position, gated SiLU MLP, KV state |
| `pllm.qwen3.v1` | dense Qwen3; pinned mini-coder-4b fixture | explicit head width, Q/K normalization, bias-free attention |
| `pllm.qwen3_5_text.v1` | pinned Qwen3.5-4B text decoder | hybrid full attention and gated-delta recurrence, convolution and recurrent state |
| `pllm.phi4_mini.v1` | pinned Phi-4-mini-instruct decoder | fused QKV, fused gate/up, partial LongRoPE |
| `pllm.gemma4_e2b_text.v1` | pinned Gemma 4 E2B text decoder | hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, double-wide suffix MLP |
| `pllm.gemma4_e4b_text.v1` | pinned Gemma 4 E4B text decoder | hybrid attention, shared KV suffix, PLE, softcap |

Describing a model is not the same as loading its checkpoint or running it
privately. Compiler support, output quality, benchmarks, and deployment are also
separate. Check [current support](/sdk/reference/status/) before choosing a model.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert {"rotary_embedding", "silu", "kv_cache_append"} <= operators
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the checked-in fixture. This creates a semantic plan only.

---

# Phi-4 mini

Fused-projection and LongRoPE semantic lowering for Phi-4-mini-instruct.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/phi4-mini/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.models.phi4-mini`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:609c000ac37d303000ede1113bc5a1df62f30e50836530ba3aec1704cf438d23`

`pllm.phi4_mini.v1` recognizes the `phi3` remote-code configuration used by `microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct` revision `cfbefacb99257ffa30c83adab238a50856ac3083`. The raw configuration SHA-256 is `ac65d86061d3d0d704ee2511fd0eb8713ef19eb6eedba17c3080a4165d5b933b`.

The adapter emits fused QKV and gate/up projections as linear operations followed by explicit slices. LongRoPE records original context, short and long factor vectors, scaling ratio, and partial rotary width. The tied output head references the token embedding matrix.

The upstream model name and adapter identity are Phi-4 mini even though the checked configuration discriminator is `phi3`. This page does not claim checkpoint import or runtime execution.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Phi-4-mini-instruct-cfbefac-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert operations["layer.0.qkv_linear"]["output_shape"] == (1, 16, 5120)
assert operations["layer.0.rope_q"]["attributes"]["rope_type"] == "longrope"
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

the pinned fixture. Lowering does not import or execute its checkpoint.

# Qwen2

Dense Qwen2 semantic lowering and its present execution boundary.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/qwen2/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.models.qwen2`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:b1c1998bca36bbce31e74429cafda255e67506c72e9628160cc84ad109879521`

`pllm.qwen2.v1` lowers bounded prefill and decode graphs for dense `qwen2` configurations. It records grouped-query attention, rotary positions, QKV bias, bias-free output and MLP projections, gated SiLU, KV-cache transitions, last-token output-head evaluation, greedy selection, and feedback.

This adapter is structurally validated rather than bound to one repository revision. Checkpoint loading and complete compiler coverage remain separate. Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is the current runtime and loopback benchmark target, not evidence that every Qwen2 semantic plan is executable.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pllm import lower_model

config = {
    "model_type": "qwen2",
    "hidden_size": 896,
    "intermediate_size": 4864,
    "num_hidden_layers": 1,
    "num_attention_heads": 14,
    "num_key_value_heads": 2,
    "vocab_size": 151936,
    "max_position_embeddings": 32768,
    "hidden_act": "silu",
    "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6,
    "rope_theta": 1000000.0,
    "tie_word_embeddings": True,
}
plan = lower_model(config, batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert operations["layer.0.k_linear"]["output_shape"] == (1, 16, 128)
assert operations["layer.0.silu"]["operator"] == "silu"
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This self-contained configuration exercises the structural Qwen2 contract without
requiring a source-checkout fixture. It creates a semantic plan only.

# Qwen3 and mini-coder

Dense Qwen3 lowering with explicit head width and Q/K normalization.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/qwen3/)

Source hash: `sha256:d882f01bf4d87fc7c158c3a5acc2aeea3f04956d19f9693dfc77932510860767`

`pllm.qwen3.v1` extends dense lowering with explicit `head_dim`, per-head Q/K RMS normalization, and configuration-controlled attention bias. Attention projection width is `num_attention_heads * head_dim`; it is not assumed equal to hidden width.

The checked fixture is `ricdomolm/mini-coder-4b` revision `c87892d046a62415a349a6b3aa244bb630fb7417`, raw configuration SHA-256 `fdbc9e0615fcb88b2cc37aa2b23fa332b3863068d50092aa6bd1e628fd187c92`. This establishes configuration parsing and semantic-plan validation only.

```python
assert operations["layer.0.q_norm"]["operator"] == "rms_norm"
assert operations["layer.0.rope_q"]["output_shape"][-1] == 128
```

# Qwen3.5

Hybrid full-attention and gated-delta semantic lowering for Qwen3.5-4B.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/models/qwen35/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.models.qwen35`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:c67f04c7a1e3cb4b24f299929fd1de3dbcf179bfb6fa5040c7e3d854c344093c`

`pllm.qwen3_5_text.v1` lowers the text decoder in `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`. The upstream configuration SHA-256 is `ddc63e1c717afa86c865bb5e01313d89d72bb53b97ad4a8a03ba8510c0621670`; the checked fixture adds one repository newline and is verified against both representations.

The plan retains the exact 3:1 linear/full layer schedule. Linear layers represent fused input projection, causal convolution state, Q/K L2 normalization, gated-delta decay and update, recurrent matrix state, and gated RMS normalization. Full-attention layers represent doubled query projection, Q/K normalization, partial multimodal rotary sections, KV state, and output gating. MTP configuration remains identity-bound but outside the base decoder graph.

These newly explicit operators currently report missing compiler coverage. Semantic lowering does not claim an executable Qwen3.5 runtime, checkpoint importer, generation quality, or protected recurrent protocol.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert operations["layer.0.linear_attention.gated_delta_rule"]["operator"] == "gated_delta_rule"
assert operations["layer.3.self_attention.q_rope"]["attributes"]["mrope_section"] == (11, 11, 10)
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the pinned fixture. Inspecting its plan is not an execution claim.

# Numerics

Understand PLLM's integer arithmetic, quantization, rounding, approximation, and overflow checks.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/numerics/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.numerics`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:2e014e5465ccb49dd79b3f2a1515bc952953f5eebeca817dcc5652cd61a42cb5`

A numeric policy records the number domain, scales, rounding, signed decoding,
modulus, wire width, coefficient limits, approximation method, and allowed error.
Its digest is part of the executable plan and related evidence.

Read [numeric semantics and model quality](/learn/numeric-semantics-and-model-quality/)
for how these choices affect overflow, token agreement, and model behavior.

The native matrix core validates dimensions and coefficients, selects a scalar or
SIMD kernel at runtime, and uses bounded integer arithmetic. Native execution does
not remove quantization error, conversions, protocol messages, or client state.

Tests must cover reference arithmetic, boundary values, overflow rejection, and a
trusted comparison for each approximation. Token agreement and task quality need
separate [end-to-end evidence](/research/evidence/).

The first locked nonlinear profile is
`pllm.numeric.silu.quadratic_q7.v1`: signed Q7 inputs in `[-128, 128]`, scale 128,
deterministic ties-to-even rounding, and a declared encoded-domain SiLU error bound
of `0.02285`. The compiler includes the numeric type in the protected plan and
rejects other numeric representations for this kernel.

## Python SDK example

```python
import numpy as np

from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor

mpc = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=0))
decoded = mpc.centered(np.array([0, 32768, 65536], dtype=np.int64))
assert decoded.tolist() == [0, 32768, -1]
```

API: [Python objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This shows center decoding in the reference arithmetic path; it does not establish full-model numeric fidelity.

---

# SiLU activation

Compile and evaluate PLLM's bounded experimental Q7 SiLU component.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/operators/activation-silu/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.operators.activation-silu`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:17d5ae9315fe707c62863428522610fb863b1e386fa04ab43f8c10fec33ba339`

PLLM implements one executable SiLU profile:
`research.single_evaluator`, using numeric graph
`pllm.numeric.silu.quadratic_q7.v1`. It encodes `[-1, 1]` at scale 128,
evaluates `x / 2 + x² / 4`, rounds ties to even, and rejects inputs outside the
locked domain. Across all 257 encoded inputs, absolute error against SiLU is at
most `0.02285`. One compiled Q7 SiLU region is capped at 128 elements in this
initial bounded slice.

The protected implementation uses modulus 257 across the bounded Q7 input and
output domains. Client wire
encodings and evaluator gates remain separate. Evaluator material is serialized
for transport within one process, registered when issued, bound to the compiled
plan, and consumed once after exact payload authentication. This is an experimental
reference component, not a complete Qwen execution profile, a cross-process replay
protocol, or a production-security claim.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
silu = next(
    operation
    for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]
    if operation["operator"] == "silu"
)
assert silu["id"] == "layer.0.silu"
assert silu["output_shape"] == (1, 16, 9728)
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the model-adapter test fixture. `ModelPlan.prefill` and its operation records are
read-only mappings.

The semantic plan preserves SiLU as an explicit operator. A separately validated
compile request can lower a bounded SiLU region to the internal native Q7 evaluator,
but PLLM does not expose that evaluator through the stable Python runtime facade.

---

# Operators

Learn how PLLM describes model operations independently of model family and runtime.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/operators/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.operators`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:3d87761d2810281ac4ca355c0f20135e88606387dd28a64e116b41075dd9e567`

Operators describe what a model does without depending on model-family names or a
specific runtime. Plans represent projections, normalization, rotary embeddings,
attention, recurrent and convolutional state, nonlinear activation, residuals,
selection, and input or output boundaries with explicit shapes and settings.

A compiler profile lists the operators it can execute. Unknown or unsupported
operations appear in `PlanCoverage` and stop compilation. PLLM never silently
replaces them with plaintext or approximate work. Research methods also use these
shared operators instead of relying on model-specific weight names.

An operator in a model plan shows only that PLLM can describe it. Read
[numeric semantics and model quality](/learn/numeric-semantics-and-model-quality/)
for why operator coverage alone is insufficient. See
[compiler](/sdk/pipeline/compiler/) for execution support and
[numerics](/sdk/build/numerics/) for integer and approximation requirements.

The bounded [SiLU activation](/sdk/build/operators/activation-silu/) is the first
operator with an experimental plan-bound protected executor. Other listed
operators remain semantic records until their compiler and runtime coverage is
implemented.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/mini-coder-4b-c87892d-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert {"linear", "rotary_embedding", "silu", "softmax"} <= operators
assert plan.coverage().complete is False
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the checked-in fixture. This inspects semantic operators; it does not establish
execution coverage.

---

# Projection and rotary variants

Represent fused projections, tensor slices, head widths, and rotary position rules.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/operators/projection-rotary/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.operators.projection-rotary`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:98f1404a999a6c764780981c84be7b83d9221bae4534d56adc7b18df104bb81e`

A fused checkpoint tensor remains one `linear` operation followed by semantic `slice` operations. This preserves storage identity without teaching a compiler model-specific tensor names. Query width, KV width, head count, and head width are independent shape facts.

`rotary_embedding` attributes distinguish ordinary RoPE, partial rotary width, multimodal sections, and LongRoPE short/long factors. A compiler must implement the declared variant or report it missing; it cannot silently substitute ordinary full-width RoPE.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Phi-4-mini-instruct-cfbefac-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operations = {operation["id"]: operation for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
assert operations["layer.0.q_slice"]["inputs"] == ("layer.0.qkv_linear",)
assert operations["layer.0.rope_q"]["attributes"]["rotary_dimensions"] == 96
assert len(operations["layer.0.rope_q"]["attributes"]["long_factor"]) == 48
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the pinned Phi-4 fixture. This reads plan records only; support still depends on
compiler coverage.

---

# Stateful recurrence

Represent convolution and recurrent state in a hybrid decoder plan.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/operators/stateful-recurrence/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.operators.stateful-recurrence`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:64d8181dacf3d471063ffc1be64deddbb01f023f0afa1bf7161beeeace345da6`

Hybrid decoders declare convolution and recurrent state separately from key/value cache state. `causal_convolution` consumes prior convolution state while `convolution_state_update` produces the next bounded state. `gated_delta_rule` consumes normalized Q/K, value, decay, beta, and prior recurrent state; `gated_delta_state_update` records the corresponding state transition.

Separate result and state-transition operations avoid implicit multi-output graph edges. Their shared inputs and attributes bind both records to one semantic update. `rms_norm_gated`, `gated_delta_decay`, and `sigmoid` retain the surrounding gating equations.

Presence in a validated plan is not implementation coverage. Current compiler profiles fail closed on these operators.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pathlib import Path

from pllm import lower_model

fixture = Path("crates/pllm-models/tests/fixtures/Qwen3.5-4B-851bf6e-config.json")
plan = lower_model(fixture.read_bytes(), batch=1, max_input_tokens=16, max_new_tokens=4)
operators = {operation["operator"] for operation in plan.prefill["operations"]}
missing = [row["operator"] for row in plan.coverage().operators if row["level"] == "missing"]
assert {"causal_convolution", "gated_delta_rule", "gated_delta_state_update"} <= operators
assert "gated_delta_rule" in missing
```

API: [Python SDK objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

Run this example from a PLLM source checkout; package installations do not include
the pinned Qwen3.5 fixture. This reports unsupported operators without executing them.

---

# Pipeline

Combine model, privacy protocol, preparation, runtime, and deployment choices in one configuration.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.pipeline`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:0aa653548a4251764aa395f5171ec48d98d5aea590cde612107eef0b8a99d83a`

A `Pipeline` records what you intend to run. Profiles provide visible defaults,
and component overrides keep their versions. The configuration digest covers
normalized values, not live connections or provider state.

Creating a pipeline does not run anything. Model lowering, research transforms,
compilation, deployment, preparation, and session creation are separate steps.
Each step returns a record or a structured error. The
[parties and offline work](/learn/parties-and-offline-work/) overview explains why
preparation and live inference remain distinct.

Run [`pllm config show`](/cli/reference/config/show/) to inspect
`examples/pllm.yaml` without loading a model or runtime.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pllm import Cpu, MaskedLinear, Model, ModelAwareCorrections, Pipeline

pipeline = Pipeline.from_profile(
    "baseline.masked_linear_cpu",
    model=Model("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct"),
    components={"linear": MaskedLinear(), "preparation": ModelAwareCorrections(), "kernels": Cpu()},
)
spec = pipeline.to_spec()
assert spec["components"]["linear"] == {"component": "pllm/masked-linear", "params": {}}
assert spec["components"]["kernels"]["params"]["threads"] == 1
```

API: [Python objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This creates public configuration only; it does not start a runtime.

---

# Preparation

Prepare one-time masked material before a private inference request starts.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/preparation/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.preparation`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:5b7483893fd1b386f018e4e615558233140714467317a5a63dbb7c6931e82cc9`

Preparation components define how one-time material is created, batched, committed,
transferred, confirmed, erased, expired, and invalidated. They also identify who
owns the material and how much can be stored. Protocol and kernel choices remain
separate.

The [parties and offline work](/learn/parties-and-offline-work/) overview explains
the role boundary. For public masked-linear inference, the client sends seed batches
to preparation. Preparation computes corrections, and inference stores them in a
sealed inventory. The client refills inventory only while idle. A restart or idle
timeout discards inventory held in memory.

Prepared material is part of the system cost. Benchmarks must state whether
preparation and loading are included in cold and warm measurements so the resulting
[research evidence](/research/evidence/) keeps that scope visible.

## Python SDK example

```python
import numpy as np

from pllm import TrustedPreprocessor

preparation = TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=7)
mask = preparation.input_mask((3,))
reconstructed = (mask.shared_mask.client.value + mask.shared_mask.server.value) % 65537
assert np.array_equal(reconstructed, mask.clear_mask_for_client)
```

API: [Python objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This creates and checks reference one-time material in process. Production use
requires a reviewed correlation protocol and separate roles.

---

# Arithmetic garbling

Mixed-modulus labels and projection gates over bounded arithmetic values.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/arithmetic/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.garbling.arithmetic`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:5d8e8cd921ebfd04bf47b410e73c52dbaa629702ba30cfa0582ef136aa064247`

Arithmetic garbling represents values with labels per modulus. Free compatible arithmetic can avoid tables; nonlinear projection reconstructs signed values jointly from a coprime residue bundle and emits output labels. Gate material is shape-bound, strictly serialized, and consumed once.

Reference exhaustive correctness, tamper rejection, plan commitments, and one-use
process-local issuance checks establish implementation behavior only. The compiler
can select the exact `research.single_evaluator` profile; the
baseline profile cannot activate it. Cryptographic review, cross-process or durable
replay protection, complete-model coverage, and deployment assurance are not
recorded.

No public Python API currently exposes the arithmetic-garbling evaluator. See
[research evidence](/research/evidence/). The evaluator remains internal to the
native compiled-plan boundary and is not part of the stable Python runtime facade.

---

# Half-gates

Boolean AND-gate representation and the obligations surrounding free-XOR circuit execution.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/half-gates/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.garbling.half-gates`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:149e42548d78ad08f4d8c22390f3013eb618a1b1af9f8d5165c41aa6e1789f21`

Half-gates reduce encrypted table material for Boolean AND gates under compatible label and hash assumptions. A component contract must bind circuit identity, wire labels, correlation assumptions, evaluator material, one-time use, serialization, and output decoding.

PLLM documents this category for composition and research mapping. Presence in the taxonomy does not state that a reviewed native implementation or executable profile exists.

No public Python API currently exposes a half-gate component. See
[research evidence](/research/evidence/) for the evidence boundary; taxonomy alone
does not provide executable SDK support.

---

# Garbling

Reference arithmetic and Boolean garbling components with explicit maturity and composition boundaries.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.garbling`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:e15bacdb7ac3166d7522e886b0b3ecf3c9b5c68fc40354f61fc4579da3a80ce2`

Garbling is a family of representations and protocols, not one interchangeable backend. PLLM records arithmetic projection gates, Boolean half-gates, lookup tables, and weighted paths separately because their domains, costs, proofs, and conversion obligations differ.

Current clean-room arithmetic work is reference-only and unreviewed. It is excluded from executable compiler profiles until protocol, transport, coverage, and assurance gates pass. See [research reproductions](/research/recipes/reproductions/).

No public Python API currently exposes garbling configuration or execution. Follow
[research reproductions](/research/recipes/reproductions/) for experimental evidence;
the unsupported SDK state is not an execution fallback.

---

# Lookup tables

Bounded function tables with explicit domains, indexing, leakage, and material size.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/lookup-tables/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.garbling.lookup-tables`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:b4de26e167a6b5b6538882089e360fdb8610b0bf90dc40bf3fd0cae0476354fa`

A lookup-table component maps a finite encoded domain to an encoded range. Its contract records signed interpretation, table cardinality, invalid indices, material ownership, one-time use, communication, and whether selection is data-oblivious under the stated threat model.

Tables are useful for nonlinearities only when domain bounds and total storage remain explicit. Approximation and model-quality evidence belong to the numeric policy, not the table name.

No public Python API currently exposes a garbled lookup-table component. See
[research evidence](/research/evidence/) for the evidence boundary; no lookup-table
component is currently published through the SDK.

---

# Weighted path

Decision-path representations for bounded piecewise or tree-structured secure evaluation.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/weighted-path/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.garbling.weighted-path`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:0e3a43bbae8b1bba9a47f12fd170c44cbc1e4c5ae3fa6629f501de693122e05c`

Weighted paths encode a sequence of predicates and selected contributions rather than a dense table. A component must state path topology, hidden and public structure, comparison semantics, branching leakage, numeric bounds, and worst-case work.

This is an extension category, not a shipped support claim. Candidate research enters through source and method records before any compiler profile can select it.

No public Python API currently exposes a weighted-path component. Follow
[research methods](/research/methods/) before treating this extension category as
an executable support claim.

---

# Protocols

See how PLLM defines parties, messages, privacy assumptions, and failure behavior.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:bc5ed0e0d4d053194e1dd12b98569bfd7e1a97a4bdad39bb09416ec7ecae5887`

A protocol defines its parties, offline and online phases, inputs, outputs,
messages, authentication, replay behavior, one-time material, visible information,
trust assumptions, and failure behavior. Model adapters and deployment policy are
separate concerns.

Start with [privacy and threat models](/learn/privacy-and-threat-models/) before
using these implementation interfaces to select a protocol.

Current protocols include [masked-linear inference](/sdk/pipeline/protocols/masked-linear/)
and experimental [garbling components](/sdk/pipeline/protocols/garbling/). Check execution
support, security review, assurance, and deployment status separately; apply the
[research evidence](/research/evidence/) rules to any supporting records.

## Python SDK example

```python
import numpy as np

from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, AuthenticationError, TrustedPreprocessor

mpc = AuthenticatedMPC(TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=2))
value = mpc.public_value(np.array([5], dtype=np.int64))
try:
    mpc.open(value.tamper_client(value_delta=1))
except AuthenticationError:
    tamper_detected = True
else:
    tamper_detected = False
assert tamper_detected
```

API: [Python objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This checks authenticated-opening failure behavior in the single-process reference
protocol; it does not start separate protocol parties.

---

# Masked linear

Prepared public-weight linear inference with seeded one-time masks and committed inventory.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/pipeline/protocols/masked-linear/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.protocols.masked-linear`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:ba67dc0c5a378cc0c277b5b680695625d31789ebb82b774a63b8ec0768a50da3`

The prepared protocol separates client, trusted preparation, and untrusted inference roles. Offline, preparation computes `W*r-s` from domain-separated client seed batches and pushes committed corrections. Online, inference atomically consumes the ticket matching `x-r` and returns `W*x-s` for client reconstruction.

Inventory identity binds model, body, stage, weight, shape, quantization, ring, modulus, wire width, and attempt budget. Rows are one-use and burned on reservation failure, cancellation, replay, or early completion. Preparation is idle during online chat.

This contract assumes protocol-following non-colluding roles and public body weights. Confidential-weight and shared-state protocols are separate.

## Python SDK example

```python
import numpy as np

from pllm import AuthenticatedMPC, TrustedPreprocessor

preparation = TrustedPreprocessor(modulus=65537, seed=3)
runtime = AuthenticatedMPC(preparation)
x = np.array([[3, -2]], dtype=np.int64)
weight = np.array([[2, 1]], dtype=np.int64)
masked_x = runtime.input(x, preparation.input_mask(x.shape))
correlation = preparation.linear_correlation(weight, x.shape)
result = runtime.centered(runtime.open(runtime.linear(masked_x, weight, correlation)))
assert result.tolist() == [[4]]
assert runtime.stats.linear_rounds == 1
```

API: [Python objects and signatures](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

This exercises prepared masked linear arithmetic in the single-process reference
protocol; it does not provide role separation or deployment assurance.

---

# Research workflows

Build, reproduce, compare, and review private-inference research with explicit stop rules.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/recipes/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.recipes`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:534dab86e03973791ceafb51bcff973c9d3946dfd9a66f6fd2417ab1b1df78ca`

A recipe records exact sources, method and component versions, model and workload
limits, environment requirements, steps, expected files, evidence, and failure
policy. Listing a recipe never runs it.

Recipes support reproducibility without making third-party repositories runtime
dependencies. PLLM implements methods independently in Python and Rust. Original
artifacts remain sources and comparison material only.

Use the pages in this section and the [research backlog](/research/backlog/) to
inspect current workflows. Recipe execution is not supported because sandboxing,
artifact identity, and result records are not yet available together.

Use the pages in this section to choose a workflow. Build and reproduction work
must stop rather than silently substituting an upstream runtime, weakening the
privacy boundary, or presenting unmatched measurements as comparable evidence.

# Native reference

Rust crates, the Python binding, data ownership, threading, and ABI support.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/reference/native/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.reference.native`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:9e528d54619b53c606bc73facfc49add51941b67a4e98bf13e995edc666de3cd`

`pllm-core` owns validated integer matrices and native execution. `pllm-models` owns model-neutral semantic lowering. Research-method crates transform semantic plans. `pllm-types` owns canonical records; `pllm-compiler` validates executable plans. `pllm-python` contains only the PyO3 boundary exposed as `pllm._native`.

The Python binding copies bytes into validated integer buffers, releases the interpreter lock around core work, and returns immutable bytes. Matrices own their validated weights; dimensions and contents cannot mutate through public Rust APIs. An executor owns its persistent Rayon pool.

The stable Python ABI starts at 3.11. No third-party native plugin ABI is currently published.

## Python SDK example

```python
from pllm.kernels import Cpu

descriptor = Cpu.describe()
assert descriptor.distribution == "pllm"
assert "cpu" in descriptor.capabilities
```

This inspects built-in metadata without loading a third-party plugin.

API: [`pllm.kernels.Cpu`](/sdk/reference/python/pllm/#objects-and-signatures)

---

# Representations

Understand how PLLM records a value's format, owner, bounds, and encoding.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/sdk/build/representations/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.representations`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:d415167b9bc0ead406e2487a40c9c6a37d401e4decf523ad43c4fe7e9981532b`

A representation states a value's number domain, shape, memory layout, owner,
bounds, encoding, and wire format. PLLM uses representations for quantized tensors,
ring elements, additive shares, masked activations, CRT residues, garbled labels,
packed prefill matrices, and one-time tickets.

Each component lists the representations it accepts and produces. Two components
can connect only through a compatible edge or an explicit
[conversion](/sdk/build/conversions/). Matching tensor shapes are not enough. Wire
format versions and ownership changes are part of the plan history.

No public Python API currently exposes representation compatibility records. See
[current Python support](/sdk/reference/status/). Current built-in descriptors do
not record representation fields; absence is not compatibility evidence.

---

# Reimplementation backlog

What PLLM will reproduce, implement, review, and measure next.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/backlog/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.backlog`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:03534dba38a58aa58afa777adb2a64477f157241e25257e4e9e90331044f0647`

PLLM tracks papers because they may improve a concrete protocol, compiler pass,
numeric primitive, or state-management boundary. A tracked paper is not a PLLM
implementation. A similar data flow is not a reproduction.

## Release-critical work

1. **Complete one executable Qwen profile.** Close every semantic, numeric,
protected, placement, state, and token-feedback gap for the preferred
`research.single_evaluator` profile. The compiler must continue to reject
partial coverage.
2. **Re-measure the current prepared runtime.** Record current-revision Qwen
prefill and decode runs with exact model, prompt length, output length,
machine, topology, cold/warm state, protocol bytes, and failure behavior.
Keep loopback, WAN, CPU, and accelerator claims separate.
3. **Tensorize and review the experimental gated-MLP component.** Extend the
compact scalar mixed-modulus program into a bounded tensor method, validate its
one-use lifecycle, authenticated plan binding, evaluator view, and memory
schedule, then obtain cryptographic review. The exact Q7 scalar schedule is not
a complete-model security result.

## Composition and search

Papers do not become isolated runtime stacks. Each reimplementation contributes
one or more components to a stable capability family: model and cache
transformations, linear or nonlinear protocols, protected representations,
conversions, preparation schemes, kernels, placement policies, assurance checks,
and benchmark objectives. Like-for-like implementations live together behind
the same typed contract; paper IDs remain provenance, not architecture.
This is an evolving taxonomy. A genuinely new semantic role, lifecycle, or type
boundary can introduce a new capability family; a new paper alone cannot.
Families may split into dedicated modules as their implementation libraries grow
without changing their stable plan contracts.

The harness will explore combinations in stages. It first rejects incompatible
numeric domains, party topologies, trust assumptions, state lifetimes, model
coverage, and devices. It then uses exhaustive or grid search for small bounded
spaces and reproducible seeded random search for larger conditional spaces.
Adaptive search can follow when enough comparable evidence exists. Every
candidate still compiles into an immutable plan and passes correctness, privacy,
execution, and evidence gates before its performance enters a comparison.

Search is multi-objective. Correctness and privacy are hard constraints; latency,
throughput, traffic, memory, preparation cost, quality, energy, and monetary cost
remain separate measurements. PLLM records a Pareto frontier for one matched
cohort rather than declaring one method universally best.

## Paper-driven work

| Priority | Source | PLLM work | Current status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R24 | Maverick | Specify delegated matrix-vector execution, LPN masking, and batch verification against the prepared public-weight stage contract; independently implement bounded native primitives and run the paper's Qwen3-4B comparison. | Planned; no PLLM implementation or reproduction |
| R23 | MPCache | Validate the existing model-neutral `DecoderPlan` transformation, then implement and measure protected cache selection under an explicitly compatible topology. | Structural plan adaptation only |
| R01-R03 | Dash, ReDash, table-free arithmetic garbling | Finish fidelity, security review, and full decoder-region composition around the existing reference primitives. | R03 source locked and adapted into the compact scalar Q7 program; not reproduced |
| R04-R11 | Garbling and decision-program foundations | Implement only the primitives required by an accepted complete-model plan, with paper-scoped tests and view definitions. | Tracked |
| R12-R18 | GPU/MPC preprocessing and nonlinear primitives | Reproduce comparable operators before considering integration; preserve each paper's party count and trust model in reports. | Tracked |
| R19-R22 | Private-transformer systems | Use as full-system comparison targets. Do not transfer their performance or security claims across different models, numeric graphs, or party topologies. | Tracked |

## Required gates

Every reimplementation advances through the same visible gates:

```text
source + version
  -> clean-room specification
  -> inspectable reference
  -> source-scope fidelity tests
  -> reusable native component
  -> typed compiler/runtime integration
  -> scoped security review
  -> matched benchmark
  -> documented promotion decision
```

Missing evidence stays missing. Functional tests do not establish privacy;
operator benchmarks do not establish complete-model execution; loopback runs do
not establish WAN performance; an adaptation does not become a reproduction
without source-scope fidelity evidence.

See [Papers](/research/papers/) for source-by-source summaries and links, the
[PLLM paper](/research/paper/) for the system contract, and
[SDK status](/sdk/reference/status/) for shipped implementation coverage.

---

# Experiments

Design reproducible experiments with fixed plans, comparable runs, and recorded failures.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/recipes/experiments/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.experiments`  
Release: `0.1.0`

Source hash: `sha256:fb74cab7b8065fcba5070e81afb8cf2a9202786a299e63581e2a8cf9027ca5fe`

Before execution, an experiment records its hypothesis, baseline, changed
component, model and workload limits, plan digests, environment, metrics, quality
requirements, assurance work, stopping rule, and expected artifacts.

Report throughput, latency, memory, CPU, online and offline network traffic, disk,
preparation work, quality, and assurance separately. Keep failed and negative

# Research papers

Prioritized paper reimplementation plan, source status, contribution summaries, and PLLM implementation boundaries.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/papers/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.papers`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:58f8a074aebb9d590958a0558c446748c9b7e2a8e68b2621f50a6e6b209b18c4`

This catalog is generated from the canonical research registry as of 2026-09-16. A tracked source, target module, or similar data flow is not evidence of implementation, reproduction, security, or benchmark parity.

R03 has a scoped clean-room component adaptation in the compact scalar Q7 program. R23 has a structural `DecoderPlan` adaptation. Neither is a paper reproduction or protected-runtime result. R01-R02 remain reference primitives only, and R24 is planned.

## Reimplementation plan

The execution order is dependency-driven rather than paper-number order. Work starts only after these prerequisites:

1. Complete one executable Qwen profile without hidden fallback regions. In progress: all prefill and decode linear operations and output heads execute as provenance-bound wrap32 regions, Qwen head-layout reshapes execute as exact checked permutations, residual additions execute in the wrap32 ring, and dense-Qwen physical-last token selection executes as an exact checked tensor region. Digest-bound centered-wrap32 Q14-to-Q7 regions freeze scale, ties-to-even rounding, reject-on-range semantics, and exact producer-consumer provenance. A compact scalar protected region composes Q7 SiLU and multiplication through an exact mixed-modulus program. Tensor protected multiplication, complete numeric scheduling, length-aware selection, whole-model scheduling, and the remaining operators remain unavailable.
2. Current prepared-runtime comparison complete: the matched four-thread experiment measured 5.229 s median full latency versus 7.886 s with one thread on the recorded loopback host.
3. Bounded Q7 SiLU review complete: exact profile authorization, process-local issued-payload binding, and single-pass Python copying are enforced; cryptographic review and cross-process replay protection remain unavailable.

Plan status as of 2026-09-17:

| Priority | Capability track | Papers | Track status |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Delegated matrix-vector execution | [R07](/research/papers/r07-slalom/), [R24](/research/papers/r24-maverick/), [R08](/research/papers/r08-carnival/), [R16](/research/papers/r16-trapdoored-matrices/) | `planned` |
| 2 | Activation approximation | [R18](/research/papers/r18-compact/) | `planned` |
| 3 | Arithmetic garbling foundation | [R03](/research/papers/r03-garbling-gadgets/), [R04](/research/papers/r04-half-gates/), [R01](/research/papers/r01-dash/), [R02](/research/papers/r02-redash/) | `partial PLLM component adaptation` |
| 4 | Protected conversions and lookup | [R06](/research/papers/r06-duty-free-bits/), [R05](/research/papers/r05-logrow/) | `planned` |
| 5 | Protected KV-cache policy | [R23](/research/papers/r23-mpcache/) | `structural adaptation only` |
| 6 | Decision structures and regional selection | [R11](/research/papers/r11-fevbdd/), [R10](/research/papers/r10-oblivious-decision-programs/), [R09](/research/papers/r09-hycc/) | `planned` |
| 7 | Preparation, compression, and acceleration | [R15](/research/papers/r15-ring-pcg/), [R20](/research/papers/r20-oblivious-compression/), [R12](/research/papers/r12-piranha/) | `planned` |
| 8 | Full-system comparison targets | [R21](/research/papers/r21-nexus/), [R22](/research/papers/r22-openbumblebee/), [R13](/research/papers/r13-sigma/), [R14](/research/papers/r14-fusefss/), [R17](/research/papers/r17-curl/) | `tracked` |
| 9 | Source-gated verifiable comparison | [R19](/research/papers/r19-open-weight-verifiable/) | `source gated` |

### 1. Delegated matrix-vector execution

**Status:** `planned`
**Papers:** [R07](/research/papers/r07-slalom/), [R24](/research/papers/r24-maverick/), [R08](/research/papers/r08-carnival/), [R16](/research/papers/r16-trapdoored-matrices/)

Establish the exact Slalom baseline, implement Maverick masking and verification, reproduce the Carnival attack, and compare trapdoored-matrix delegation.

Module homes:

- `pllm-core::delegation::{masked_matvec,lpn_mask,batch_verify,trapdoored_matrix}`
- `pllm-assurance::attacks::carnival_projection`

### 2. Activation approximation

**Status:** `planned`
**Papers:** [R18](/research/papers/r18-compact/)

Reproduce Compact fitting and add immutable approximation profiles for SiLU, GeLU, and related bounded activations.

Module homes:

- `pllm-core::activation::piecewise`
- `pllm-compiler::approximation::{fit,profile}`

### 3. Arithmetic garbling foundation

**Status:** `partial PLLM component adaptation`
**Papers:** [R03](/research/papers/r03-garbling-gadgets/), [R04](/research/papers/r04-half-gates/), [R01](/research/papers/r01-dash/), [R02](/research/papers/r02-redash/)

Complete reviewed arithmetic and Boolean foundations, tensor evaluation, and residue scaling before full decoder-region composition.

Module homes:

- `pllm-garble::{arithmetic,boolean,half_gates,projection,label_tensor,rns_scale}`

### 4. Protected conversions and lookup

**Status:** `planned`
**Papers:** [R06](/research/papers/r06-duty-free-bits/), [R05](/research/papers/r05-logrow/)

Add typed Boolean-to-arithmetic conversion and efficient protected lookup only where an accepted complete-model plan requires them.

Module homes:

- `pllm-garble::conversion`
- `pllm-garble::lookup`

### 5. Protected KV-cache policy

**Status:** `structural adaptation only`
**Papers:** [R23](/research/papers/r23-mpcache/)

Validate the existing model-neutral transform, then reproduce protected static and dynamic cache selection in an explicitly compatible topology.

Module homes:

- `pllm-models::cache::{policy,full,static_eviction,dynamic_eviction}`

### 6. Decision structures and regional selection

**Status:** `planned`
**Papers:** [R11](/research/papers/r11-fevbdd/), [R10](/research/papers/r10-oblivious-decision-programs/), [R09](/research/papers/r09-hycc/)

Represent public functions compactly, add protected traversal where justified, and select legal protocol regions with conversion costs included.

Module homes:

- `pllm-compiler::{decision_diagram,region_selection,conversion_costs}`
- `pllm-garble::branching`

### 7. Preparation, compression, and acceleration

**Status:** `planned`
**Papers:** [R15](/research/papers/r15-ring-pcg/), [R20](/research/papers/r20-oblivious-compression/), [R12](/research/papers/r12-piranha/)

Compare correlation generation, bounded wire compression, and GPU kernels after exact CPU components establish correctness baselines.

Module homes:

- `pllm-core::correlation`
- `pllm-core::codec::oblivious_linear_code`
- `pllm-core::kernels::gpu`

### 8. Full-system comparison targets

**Status:** `tracked`
**Papers:** [R21](/research/papers/r21-nexus/), [R22](/research/papers/r22-openbumblebee/), [R13](/research/papers/r13-sigma/), [R14](/research/papers/r14-fusefss/), [R17](/research/papers/r17-curl/)

Reproduce unlike HE, two-party, FSS, and wavelet systems in isolated adapters without importing their topology or claims into the default profile.

Module homes:

- `protocol capability family`
- `preparation capability family`
- `activation capability family`
- `kernel capability family`

### 9. Source-gated verifiable comparison

**Status:** `source gated`
**Papers:** [R19](/research/papers/r19-open-weight-verifiable/)

Acquire and lock the complete protocol and artifact before specifying or implementing its open-weight verification boundary.

Module homes:

- `protocol open-weight verification capability`
- `verification model-owner setup capability`

Paper names remain provenance. Implementations live in capability-oriented modules so compatible alternatives can be composed and benchmarked through the same plan slots.

# R01: Dash: Accelerating Distributed Private Convolutional Neural Network Inference with Arithmetic Garbled Circuits

Arithmetic garbling and LabelTensors provide the foundation for offline preparation and local encoded public-weight evaluation. PLLM status: reference primitive only.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/papers/r01-dash/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.papers.r01-dash`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:094756837e207bf9ad8a47adc2252823f3d129e0e49429fcc5cb52cfac13682f`

**Status:** `reference primitive only`
**Year:** 2024
**Authors:** Jonas Sander, Sebastian Berndt, Ida Bruhns, Thomas Eisenbarth
**External source:** [Dash: Accelerating Distributed Private Convolutional Neural Network Inference with Arithmetic Garbled Circuits](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.06361v2)

## Source contribution

Arithmetic garbling and LabelTensors provide the foundation for offline preparation and local encoded public-weight evaluation.

## PLLM perspective

Implement affine-label arithmetic, constant multiplication with the required algebraic preconditions, projections and tensorized evaluation. Preserve the original circuit functionality before adapting to transformers.

Prior single-server, model-aware and tenx archives contain adaptations, not a reproduced Dash release.

PLLM has related clean-room reference primitives only. They are not a paper reproduction, reviewed protected runtime, or complete-model result.

The source's boundary remains binding: Do not inherit malicious security by importing kernels: the paper discusses additional integrity mechanisms and trusted-hardware or cryptographic configurations.

## PLLM modules and documentation

Target module identifiers: `garble.affine_label`, `kernel.label_tensor`, `gate.projection`. These identifiers describe scoped work unless this page explicitly links an implementation source. Dependencies: R03, R04.

**Status:** `reference primitive only`
**Year:** 2025
**Authors:** Felix Maurer, Jonas Sander, Thomas Eisenbarth
**External source:** [ReDASH: Fast and efficient Scaling in Arithmetic Garbled Circuits for Secure Outsourced Inference](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.14489v1)

## Source contribution

ReDASH generalizes residue-number-system scaling and uses ScaleQuant+ to reduce encoded-inference overhead.

## PLLM perspective

Implement signed base extension, the published scaling gadget and its quantization policy as separately versioned components. Expose exact and approximate semantics explicitly.

Only researched previously; earlier CRT kernels did not implement full ReDASH scaling.

PLLM has related clean-room reference primitives only. They are not a paper reproduction, reviewed protected runtime, or complete-model result.

# R03: Garbling Gadgets for Boolean and Arithmetic Circuits

Arithmetic garbling provides free additions and specialized gadgets, with a stated symmetric-primitive security model. PLLM status: PLLM component adaptation.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/papers/r03-garbling-gadgets/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.papers.r03-garbling-gadgets`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:24dd1d6b184130011f70fd1f3bffd1a94a22e18d0ab1b2e296f32b1af963c1d7`

**Status:** `PLLM component adaptation`
**Year:** 2016
**Authors:** Marshall Ball, Tal Malkin, Mike Rosulek
**External source:** [Garbling Gadgets for Boolean and Arithmetic Circuits](https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/969)

## Source contribution

Arithmetic garbling provides free additions and specialized gadgets, with a stated symmetric-primitive security model.

## PLLM perspective

Create a reviewed arithmetic-label core with modulus-specific offsets, permitted constant operations, projection and mixed-modulus gadgets. Keep offsets opaque.

Affine-label arithmetic exists in archived references; no proof-equivalent native port has been established.

PLLM uses the source-locked projection and CRT constructions in a clean-room compact scalar Q7 program. This is a scoped component adaptation, not a paper reproduction, reviewed protected runtime, tensor method, or complete-model result.

The source's boundary remains binding: Functionality alone does not validate affine-label correlations or an arbitrary hash replacement. Reject unsupported non-unit constants or lower them through justified gadgets.

## PLLM modules and documentation

Target module identifiers: `garble.arithmetic`, `gate.mixed_modulus`. These identifiers describe scoped work unless this page explicitly links an implementation source. Dependencies: None.

## Source contribution

Half-gates reduce AND-gate communication while remaining compatible with free XOR.

## PLLM perspective

Implement Boolean label ownership, free XOR and half-gates using a precisely documented reviewed hash instantiation. Batch native cryptographic operations and expose circuit I/O conversions.

The lookup construction reduces the number of security-parameter-sized ciphertexts; total communication retains a table-data term.

# R23: MPCache: MPC-Friendly KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Private Large Language Model Inference

MPCache evaluates MPC-friendly static and dynamic KV-cache eviction in a three-party SecretFlow/SPU setting; its artifact focuses state selection and operator costs. PLLM status: PLLM reimplementation.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/papers/r23-mpcache/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.papers.r23-mpcache`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:82a07794a6271b59d14e810bfedef103c31e14bfbc8c42ed752b15900d02d0f4`

**Status:** `PLLM reimplementation`
**Year:** 2025
**Authors:** Wenxuan Zeng, Ye Dong, Jinjin Zhou, Junming Ma, Jin Tan, Runsheng Wang, Meng Li
**External source:** [MPCache: MPC-Friendly KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Private Large Language Model Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06807v2)

## Source contribution

MPCache evaluates MPC-friendly static and dynamic KV-cache eviction in a three-party SecretFlow/SPU setting; its artifact focuses state selection and operator costs.

## PLLM perspective

Reproduce cached generation and use its explicit KV state as a comparison oracle for PLLM decoder state without inferring complete protected boundary coverage.

No MPCache reproduction has been executed. Current PLLM work is a structural DecoderPlan adaptation only.

PLLM implements only a structural `DecoderPlan` adaptation. It does not reproduce MPCache's three-party protected runtime. Fidelity, protected execution, assurance, and matched benchmark status remain unchecked.

The source's boundary remains binding: Three online semi-honest parties and incomplete protected-boundary evidence are incompatible with the one-evaluator complete-model target.

## PLLM modules and documentation

Target module identifiers: `protocol.mpcache`, `state.secret_shared_kv`, `gate.mpcache_attention`. These identifiers describe scoped work unless this page explicitly links an implementation source. Dependencies: None.

- [Research backlog](/research/backlog/)
- [Reimplementation backlog](/research/backlog/)
- [Clean-room workflow](/research/clean-room/)
- [PLLM method status](/research/methods/)
- [Decoder plan usage](/sdk/plans/)
- [MPCache structural adaptation source](https://github.com/blairhudson/pllm/blob/main/crates/pllm-models/src/cache.rs)

## Backlog

This source is assigned to reimplementation priority 5, **Protected KV-cache policy**. Its source-registry order is 23. Follow current gates and unfinished work in the [research backlog](/research/backlog/).

# R24: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation

Maverick delegates matrix-vector multiplication with transparent preprocessing, information-theoretic batch verification, and LPN-based pseudorandom input masking while adding virtually no server-side verification overhead. PLLM status: planned.

[View canonical HTML](https://pllm.run/research/papers/r24-maverick/)

Document ID: `pllm.docs.research.papers.r24-maverick`  
Release: `0.1.0`  
Build: `sha256:06781cb06588c2919922b5252154662ef566cf6cbec9ad8049f32aa70887b75e`  
Source hash: `sha256:7258e6ba301518570a97f05c659f6b2aafdb70692d8827c57cef90c1911bb3f4`

**Status:** `planned`
**Year:** 2026
**Authors:** Ben Merbaum, Mohammad Amin Raeisi, Wenhao Wang, Charalampos Papamanthou, Katerina Sotiraki, Fan Zhang
**External source:** [Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10264v1)

## Source contribution

Maverick delegates matrix-vector multiplication with transparent preprocessing, information-theoretic batch verification, and LPN-based pseudorandom input masking while adding virtually no server-side verification overhead.

## PLLM perspective

The delegated linear operation is close to PLLM's prepared public-weight path, but the protocols and claims are not interchangeable. PLLM currently uses one-time masks and preloaded `W·r-s` corrections under an honest-but-curious, non-colluding preparation/inference assumption. It does not implement Maverick's verification or LPN masking construction.

An independent PLLM reproduction should first specify the paper's exact matrix-vector, masking, and verification interfaces; implement bounded native reference primitives; and compare them with the same Qwen3-4B workload and party/resource accounting. Similar data flow is not evidence of implementation, correctness, privacy, or verifiability.

This work is planned. PLLM does not yet implement Maverick's delegation, LPN masking, or batch verification, and claims no reproduction or matched benchmark.

The source's boundary remains binding: The paper's input-privacy and verifiability claims depend on its exact transparent-preprocessing, LPN, and verification constructions. Similarity to PLLM's prepared matrix path does not transfer those claims to PLLM.

## PLLM modules and documentation

Target module identifiers: `protocol.delegated_matvec`, `gate.batch_verification`, `preparation.lpn_masking`. These identifiers describe scoped work unless this page explicitly links an implementation source. Dependencies: None.

- [Research backlog](/research/backlog/)
- [Reimplementation backlog](/research/backlog/)
- [Clean-room workflow](/research/clean-room/)
- [Masked linear protocol](/sdk/pipeline/protocols/masked-linear/)

## Backlog

This source is assigned to reimplementation priority 1, **Delegated matrix-vector execution**. Its source-registry order is 24. Follow current gates and unfinished work in the [research backlog](/research/backlog/).
